items.title: 52115_Danny Barker oral history interview
items.q: And he met this woman, this fast woman there named Ruby.

ctx.x: There was a special section in New Orleans that was called the Tenderloin, over at Basin Street... You hear "The Basin Street Blues," says, "Why don't you come along with me." And over there you went... You went into there because there was no curfew. I keep repeating that there was no curfew in New Orleans. And the city decided to put all these non-conforming people over in that section, and do what you want, 24 hours around the clock, but just stay over in there amongst your bunch.

My father used to deliver this wine, and heavy liquors, whiskey and beers, other stimulants, over to these joints. And all the joints, most of them had a piano. And he could play a little piano. And he met this woman, this fast woman there named Ruby. She had seen his mule, him and this mule. And he played these Blues on this piano, and he was pretty nice to look at -- and she inveigled him why he wanted to be foolin' around with that mule and that old truck when he could be over there. And the usual procedure…
